shared_text:
The flight. A narrow-body airliner on an airline flight, on a visual approach to an airport in controlled airspace. Visual conditions, with tailwinds on the approach.

The crew. The first officer was the pilot flying and the captain the pilot monitoring. The captain had about 106 hours on type, all of them in the previous 90 days.

What happened. Air traffic control cleared the aircraft for a visual approach. The autopilot was engaged and was flying the turn onto final. Because of the tailwinds, the aircraft overshot the final approach course. The captain told the first officer, who disconnected the autopilot to correct back towards the course. In the turn back, the bank went past 30 degrees, to an estimated 38 to 40 degrees; the first officer had not intended this. As the captain told the first officer about the bank, the "bank angle" aural alert sounded. The first officer corrected the bank immediately, and the approach continued.
safe_outcome: The aircraft landed normally. There was no conflict with other traffic. No one was hurt and the aircraft was not damaged.
bad_outcome: Another aircraft was descending nearby. Both crews received TCAS resolution advisories and followed them, and the aircraft passed about 300 feet vertically and half a mile apart. A flight attendant on this aircraft was thrown against a galley cart during the manoeuvre and received a minor injury.
bracket_fill: [climbing / descending / crossing] = descending; [this aircraft] = this aircraft
notes: The source narrative is only about 80 words; the shared text reaches the range by stating each reported fact in full, with nothing added. Nothing to remove under rule 3: the report has no reflection section. 'By accident' was rendered as 'which the first officer had not intended'. Moved to the safe ending (rule 5): 'A normal landing occurred'. Removed under rule 6: the airport. Judgement calls: the reporter is coded only as captain, not as pilot flying or monitoring; the first officer is taken as pilot flying because the first officer disconnected the autopilot and flew the correction; 'about 106 hours on type, all in the previous 90 days' follows from the coded type and 90-day hours being the same (106.12); time of day is not given, so it is not stated. Bracket 'descending' because the aircraft overshot the final approach course, beyond which other approach traffic would be descending; no traffic is mentioned in the report.
